merger_description:
Kanda Healthcare Pty Ltd (**Kanda**), together with Kanda Foundation Limited (**Kanda Foundation**) and Kanda Management Services Pty Ltd, propose to acquire 100% of the assets of the disability accommodation and support services business known as Connecting Families (**Connecting Families**) through a business sale deed (the **Acquisition**).

Kanda is an Australian care provider supplying a broad range of care services, including aged care, in-home care, disability support, community nursing and children, youth and family services, in metro and regional communities across Australia. Kanda is a registered provider under the National Disability Insurance Scheme (**NDIS**), providing disability accommodation and support services to NDIS participants, including in NSW, Qld, SA and the ACT.

Kanda is controlled by Genesis Capital, an Australian-based private equity firm that invests in businesses operating in the healthcare sector. Kanda Foundation is an Australian public company limited by guarantee and a registered charity.

Connecting Families is owned and operated by Connecting Families Group Pty Ltd and its subsidiaries, Connecting Families Disability Services Pty Ltd, Connecting Families Centred Care Pty Ltd and Connecting Families Shared Services Pty Ltd. Connecting Families is also a registered provider under the NDIS and delivers disability accommodation and support services to NDIS participants in NSW, Qld, SA and the ACT.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information, the ACCC considers that the Acquisition is
unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of competition given:
a. there is a small horizontal overlap between Kanda and
Connecting Families in some of the local areas in which they
both supply NDIS-funded supported independent living and
accommodation services, and community support services,
in SA, NSW and Qld
b. there are alternative providers of NDIS-funded supported
independent living and accommodation services, and
community support services, in the local areas in which
Connecting Families supplies services in SA, NSW and Qld.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
